question.text: Per SEBI ICDR Regulations, a 'Retail Individual Investor' on SSE is defined by which applied-value threshold?

answer.text: An individual investor applying or bidding for specified securities for a value of not more than INR 2 lakhs
An individual investor applying for specified securities for a value of not more than INR 10 lakhs
An individual investor applying for any amount, provided they are above 18 years of age
An institutional investor holding assets under management exceeding INR 500 cr

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.1.4, a Retail Individual Investor is an individual who applies or bids for specified securities for a value of not more than INR 2 lakhs. Above this, they are classified as Non-Institutional Investor (unless QIB-qualified). The Trap: Option B (Rs 10 lakh) is a common mis-remembering. Option C ignores the amount cap entirely. Option D describes QIB/HNI territory, not retail. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to XII (Securities Markets), X-A (IA) where investor categorisation drives suitability. SIAs track investor-category mix in SSE subscriber disclosures. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Retail participation in ZCZP or SSE equity issuances is limited — but a sudden spike in retail subscribers may signal marketing issues. Flag to the SSE compliance team; not an SIA scope item but useful context for governance-risk narrative.
